format: Sequences of acts on one namespace registry (patterns/namespace), each step with the verdict the pattern's Deciding a statement gives it: 'accepted', or the refusal code. Every sequence starts at an empty registry whose log id is `registry`. A step's `at` is the registry's clock, in Unix seconds. A `statement` is a claim, grant or transfer the registry decides and, if accepted, appends; a `release` is a catalog release a verifier decides against the registry's state as its log recorded it at the release's `released_at`, each accepted entry recorded at its step's `at`, and appends nothing; a release step's `index` is the text of the index the release names, as the verifier fetched it, and every release a sequence accepts is one its verifier holds from then on; a `ruling` is the hub owner's, recorded in the log. Each signature's `by` names the key it says it was made with; in one step it was made with another, and is refused. `state` is every listed namespace's state after the last step: status, holder and grants by key name, an absent grants meaning none. `enrolled` is every identity the registry's hub has enrolled, by key name, with its kind; any other key is not enrolled. `never_claimable` holds the place and issuer codes these vectors use, while a registry refuses every such code (schemas/names), not only these.
keys: Every key is named as in vectors/fixed-form-statements.json, which holds its seed, public key and fingerprint; a key's fingerprint is what a field holds.
made_with: github.com/cloudflare/circl v1.6.5, FIPS 204 deterministic signing, as vectors/fixed-form-statements.json

sequences.case: the first claim takes the name; a second claim of it, by anyone, is refused, and the first claim's own bytes sent again are a replay
reserved names, place and issuer codes, names confusable with a reserved name, and names outside the grammar are refused, and none is held after

a service identity, an identity the hub never enrolled, a claim signed by someone other than its holder, a signature made by another key than the one it names, another registry's claim, a stale claim and a malformed time are each refused, and the name stays unheld
a transfer signed by one side is refused; signed by both it moves the namespace and ends the outgoing holder's grants; the outgoing holder then holds nothing, and a service identity cannot take it on
a rotation signed by both keys moves the namespace to the incoming key and keeps its grants; the outgoing key can no longer act, and a grantee from before the rotation still publishes
a retirement names no incoming holder; once retired, the name is never claimed again, by its last holder or anyone, and nothing is granted, released or reassigned under it

ruling.reason: a ruling never un-retires a namespace

sequences.case: a frozen namespace accepts no grant and is still held; a reassignment moves it and ends its grants, and the earlier holder can no longer act; a reassignment only to an enrolled user, and no ruling on a name nobody claimed

ruling.reason: a dispute over who holds the name
the holder's key was lost; the name goes to the person the decision names
a reassignment to an identity this hub never enrolled
a reassignment to a service identity
a freeze of a name nobody claimed

sequences.case: a release verifies only while its signer is the holder or a publish grantee; withdrawing the grant ends it, and a namespace nobody claimed has no releases

a release is judged against the namespace's state at its own released_at, as the log records it: a release the holder's old key made before a rotation, and one made before a transfer, still verify after it; the old key cannot release after the rotation; a back-dated release can neither come after a later one nor give a release a second index; and a release dated beyond the replay window is not yet decidable

a release continues the one before it: its number is the next, its previous is that release's index, its released_at is no earlier, and its index keeps every ref, a retired one still retired; an index whose text is not the digest the release signed is malformed
